messages:
leah: heads up — customer ACME-4321 opened an escalation: p99 jumped ~1.3s and sporadic 502s for EU users starting 2026-03-15T14:20Z. They attached sample trace id trace-e2b9c and request headers.
omar: can you paste the trace and a minimal repro? need to know hosted vs dedicated and account plan.
divya: theyare on Hosted (ACME-4321). Repro curl they sent: 
```
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -H "X-Trace-Id: trace-e2b9c" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-rl","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":12}'
```
kai: pasted our trace for trace-e2b9c from jaeger: 
```
trace-e2b9c
  edge-eu-02 -> 9ms
  router-eu -> 25ms
  region-decider -> 7ms
  compat-fallback -> 0ms
  peering-us-west -> 860ms
  model-us-west-2 -> 315ms
  total -> 1216ms
```

kai: you can see the massive jump at peering-us-west. should have stayed within eu-west-1.
jen: looking at tenant routing config: ACME pinned to eu-west-1 but recent fallback pool (compat-global) includes us-west as an available region. there was an autoscale glitch that briefly moved traffic into compat-global.
leah: i replicated quickly with a small load generator (50 concurrency) and region header set to eu-west-1. ~4% of requests hit us-west path. repro steps i used: 
```
# quick repro
for i in $(seq 1 50); do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" -H "X-Trace-Sample: repro-$i" \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-rl","prompt":"ping","max_tokens":6}' &\
done; wait
# then search traces for peering-us-west hits
rg "repro-" | rg peering-us-west
```
omar: deploy-bot shows PR #5032 (route matcher precedence tweaks) merged at 2026-03-15T14:17Z. that change simplified matchers and removed an explicit "pool.region == tenant.region" condition from compat-global fallback.
oncall-bot: alert: capacity downscale event detected for eu-prod at 2026-03-15T14:18Z; autoscaler bumped fallback usage to compat-global for short window.
divya: hypothesis: under a brief capacity pressure the new matcher precedence allowed compat-global to match before region-restricting guards, letting a fraction of requests egress to us-west.
jen: logs from region-decider around the window: 
```
[14:20:12Z] region-decider: tenant=ACME-4321 target=eu-west-1 pool=eu-prod
[14:20:12Z] autoscaler: eu-prod slots low -> invoke fallback
[14:20:12Z] compat-matcher: matched pool=compat-global (id=pg-77)
[14:20:12Z] egress: selected peering-us-west route
```

kai: i ran a focused repro where i artificially reduced local slots on eu-prod, and i get repro id repro-19 that shows the us-west hop. trace snippet: 
```
repro-19
  edge-eu-02 -> 11ms
  router-eu -> 24ms
  compat-fallback -> 0ms
  peering-us-west -> 872ms
  model-us-west-2 -> 320ms
  total -> 1227ms
```
leah: customer impact: higher p99 latency and a few 502s reported. billing unaffected; SLA risk but short window. acme asked for immediate mitigation and ETA.
omar: immediate actions i propose: 1) hotfix rollback of PR #5032 to restore explicit region check in compat matcher, 2) apply a tenant-level route override pinning ACME to eu-prod for 2h, 3) raise eu-prod autoscale floor to avoid micro fallbacks.
divya: i'll open hotfix PR and the override now. also recommend adding a unit/regression test that verifies compat matchers never select cross-region pools for region-pinned tenants.
oncall-bot: hotfix PR #5075 created and rolled to canary. route override applied to ACME-4321 (expires in 2h). autoscale floor increased for eu-prod.
jen: we should also instrument a new metric: cross_region_egress_rate by tenant-region and alert if >0.5% over 5m.
marco: (ops) can we confirm customer sees improvement?
tracebot: canary metrics: ACME-4321 shows 0 cross-region egress after override; p99 returned to baseline by 14:28Z.
leah: good. postmortem owners and actions: root cause writeup (owner: jen), regression test & repro harness (owner: divya), cross-region metric & alert (owner: kai), customer comms draft (owner: leah).
omar: customer notification sent with summary and ETA for full postmortem in 48h. they replied asking to be alerted if any fallback uses non-EU pools.
leah: noted. i'll add a temporary dashboard for ACME to monitor egress region usage and share with their SRE.
tracebot: closing note: hotfix reverted matcher change in canary, no further cross-region hits observed for ACME-4321.
leah: thanks team, keep the thread updated if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
